passages.provision_quote: Following the implementation of the minimum wage increase specified in subparagraph (F) of paragraph (2) of subdivision (b), on or before August 1 of that year, and on or before each August 1 thereafter, the Director of Finance shall calculate an adjusted minimum wage. The calculation shall increase the minimum wage by the lesser of 3.5 percent and the rate of change in the averages of the most recent July 1 to June 30, inclusive, period over the preceding July 1 to June 30, inclusive, period for the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics nonseasonally adjusted United States Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (U.S. CPI-W). The result shall be rounded to the nearest ten cents ($0.10). Each adjusted minimum wage increase calculated under this subdivision shall take effect on the following January 1.
passages.note: Chaptered text; the operative Section 1182.12 raises the floor in dated steps to fifteen dollars and then indexes it annually to the CPI-W with no further vote.

rows.reasoning: Gipson voted Aye on Assembly final passage of SB 3 (2015-2016), whose operative Labor Code section raises the state minimum wage in dated annual steps to fifteen dollars an hour and then provides that "the Director of Finance shall calculate an adjusted minimum wage" by the U.S. CPI-W, where "Each adjusted minimum wage increase calculated under this subdivision shall take effect on the following January 1." That matches both clauses of the rung reading "Raise the wage floor and tie it to the cost of living, so it rises automatically each year without new legislation", and the standing index excludes the rung that would "adjust it only when lawmakers vote to." The bill's titled, dominant subject is the minimum wage and its sick-leave section is pegged to that same wage schedule, so the vote is single-subject enough to carry a chair, and the 48-26 tally is not near-unanimous.
